title: How do you sell a game on Steam that uses AI-Generated artwork without being thrown into the pits of hell and refunded to oblivion? Any tips or experience are welcome? I'm an old-school game dev just jumping into this AI assisted world.
author: chaicpp
selftext:
We all know the game needs to be fun and well polished, let's just say YOUR game has that covered for the sake of this conversation. How do you sell it without getting refunded or review bombed? 

Apparently people can buy your game and within minutes request a refund just because they didn't like it, oh and leave a bad review. I found this one psychopath on X demanding a developer prove the game does not use AI content or else in their words: "the witch hunt will continue!!!". Keep in mind, the devs didn't use AI and were quite "anti". 

I'm genuinely curious in finding out what you all do to get by all this and sell to a proper audience. 

I thought of just translating my game to Chinese, Japanese, Spanish, and Korean and avoid English, DESPITE being a language I understand and speak comfortably. Almost ALL witch hunt related messages and reviews were from English speakers. A lot of Asian games that use AI even have overwhelmingly positive reviews.

Who knows, maybe Asian devs will stop translating games in order to avoid the witch hunt and even create their own storefront.

I know I could just "ignore the haters", but when it's time to sell, not sure what to do. What are your thoughts?

comments.author: TartNo3610
comments.body:
You don’t lol. Everyone is hating on AI. For some of us we can bring great ideas to life with it. Until things change you’ll have to have such an amazing game to get past the hate and even then people will hate religiously. 

It seems to easy to be with AI, and this is the catch.

replies.author: chaicpp
replies.body:
That's too bad, but I understand your point of view. You know what hurts? I know most of the haters will get old or naturally die off and once that happens, I'm also too old or not here anymore, but future generations will enjoy making games comfortably with this technology. 

I'm not a one shot kind of person, I'm playing around with Minimax and generating videos in order to make sprite sheets, cleaning them, etc. It's a lot of fun. Much respect to the craft of artist but not everybody can afford paying what they ask for. I've had mfers even scam me. 

Argh, sucks. Thanks for the reply!

replies.author: affabledrunk
replies.body: You don’t have to wait for haters to get old and die, the tide is already turning, they’re already less vocal than they were 3 months ago I would bet they by mid 2027 the haters will be all but be over since literally every single game on steam will be AI developed.

replies.author: chaicpp
replies.body:
You know, I read somebody else on this sub mentioning the same thing. Not sure if you saw that post about how 80% of Japanese devs are using AI? If you read the comments, there was a lot of support, which was surprising to me. 

I hope you're right, if you put work into this all this, you can make some really awesome stuff.

replies.author: affabledrunk
replies.body: Yeah. You can see it happen in real time. And if it’s happening inside Reddit which is the main anti-ai zealot hive, it will be happening much more in the real world

replies.author: khodakk
replies.body: i feel like there could be a market place for ai games for now. like a new game market place where you don’t need to disclose cause the understanding is AI is used for all the games. would just need a few games to go viral and then people will use it cause the games can’t wouldn’t be sold anywhere else

replies.author: mankrip
replies.body: That's the Epic Games Store.

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body: There is, and it's not Steam.

comments.author: Manifesto-Engine
comments.body: Make the game but put love into it, ai or not.

replies.author: chaicpp
replies.body: That's true, but I've seen beautiful games that disclose the use of AI and the same groups of Anti clansmen seem to attack the project. But it's true that most of all put love into the project.

replies.author: Manifesto-Engine
replies.body: Those vile dogs shouldn't be anyway near a keyboard. They don't actually care about art just that more can do their own thing now and they hate that. I'm thinking the best response to this may be custom sites tailored to the game itself. They have zero control over that. :)

replies.author: chaicpp
replies.body:
Hmmm, think about it, you're right about a custom tailored site. Didn't Minecraft do the same? The only disadvantage I can find is some people will be afraid of downloading from a place they don't trust, but I 100% think it's worth a try. 

Back in the days it was like this. Hey that's not a bad idea :)

replies.author: Manifesto-Engine
replies.body: Think it's time for custom sites to make a come back for games. :)

replies.author: Strict-Broccoli-8877
replies.body:
Yes, it's a bad idea. A terrible idea. The idea really couldn't be any worse.

75% of PC game sales are done on Steam. If you don't happen to be the Epic store, you're site will get fractions of a percent of the views your product page would get on Steam. You would have sold a thousand copies? Now it's one. A hundred thousand, a real success story? It's 100 sold on your own site, if you are lucky.

"But Minecraft..." You are not Minecraft.

replies.author: chaicpp
replies.body:
This is the exact mentality that explains why we're using the same platforms and services for years. "Why re-create the wheel", "You're not minecraft". "This is a bad idea even though you never tried it". 

Steam has millions of players but these platforms are well designed rat races which makes it really difficult standing out, and I'm not saying not give that a try too.

I respect your opinion, but I prefer people try things even though they sound "stupid" or "crazy". It cost nothing to put up a website, so fuck it. 

We've got AI that can make a nice looking sites in minutes and now we're going to limit ourselves. Sorry but doesn't make sense to me.

replies.author: Strict-Broccoli-8877
replies.body: Dude - if you want to sell your cabbages, you do so at the cabbage market. You are free to try to sell them in your attic where nobody besides you has ever been, it's just an obviously bad choice.

comments.author: RUSuper
comments.body: I mean... haters gonna hate? Disclose it on steam that you used an AI for it and try to make it as good as possible for people who don't mind AI to actually enjoy it. It's the only thing that is in your control 🤷‍♂️

replies.author: chaicpp
replies.body: Thanks for the reply. It seems the overall sentiment so far is focus on disclosure. Still a scary process. If I were an artist, I'd probably would just make my own art if I'm 100% honest, but I suck at art.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body: none of the above happened me but my games haven't seen much traffic period. whenever I share my games here, I also get downvoted lol.

replies.author: chaicpp
replies.body:
Not sure why some of the replies are getting downvoted. It's definitely not me, I appreciate everybody's replies.

I would have thought sharing a game on this thread would get more support, you surprised me, sorry to hear that.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
well, to be fair, it doesn't cost me anything to mention my games on reddit so there is that

but yeah, game marketing is a whole another challenge and it is not a fun challenge. I wouldn't go as far as saying "people don't want you to succeed" but they definitely feel more comfortable roasting you or show indifference. 

in the end, it is a fair game because it is not like creators share their success when they do succeed... its good I guess

replies.author: JorgitoEstrella
replies.body:
Gonna be honest your last post looks like the alpha of the alpha.

I like posts when people ask something and others discuss tools and workflows but when someone claims "hey what do you think of my game" and its slop that looks like it was made in 1 hour max it gets tiring.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
no worries. I am familiar with this sub operates

for example, I have been posting my latest project for 2-3 weeks now so it is definitely not "made in 1 hour max"

you can even try to prompt for an hour and you wouldnt get something similar. 

based on your assessment, I doubt that you work on projects much but its okay. i.e. I actually shared my project in another dev's post and the immediate response went to how the realtime destruction is  handled, not really visual quality

we are basically in an environment where everyone think everyone else is making slops 

in reality, many of us here are indie indie so... expectation and reality

comments.author: EnumeratedArray
comments.body:
Just be completely transparent and honest about how you've used AI.

From what I've seen, people don't like buying a game they thought didn't use AI and then finding out it did.

People who don't want to play games made with AI will just avoid it with the right disclaimers. People will refund and review bomb if you intentionally mislead them.

replies.author: chaicpp
replies.body: You're right about that, not disclosing the use of AI is even worst. Still scary releasing a game that even mentions those two letters, but you're right about that.

replies.author: Reasonable-Plum7059
replies.body: You just want to make life of “those” easier

replies.author: PhantomZenithOrigin
replies.body: Or just make sure that by Steam's own guidelines you don't qualify for the AI disclosure so you can honestly declare no AI, and if anyone points anything out you can choose to not answer them or simply point at Steam's own guidelines and say you're in adherence with their AI disclosure and not discuss it further with that person.

comments.author: sircontagious
comments.body: If your game looks obvious enough that its ai made then you haven't polished it yet.

replies.author: JMGameDev
replies.body: Not really, some artstyles are just known to be AI favoured, to the point real people creating in that same style are being accused of being AI. Being polished does not equal changing your entire artstyle to avoid styles AI are good at

comments.author: Every-Prize4720
comments.body: by making actual good polished game.

comments.author: Eisenkopf69
comments.body: Completely your thing whatever you decide. Don't play into the creeps' hands. Let them do what they want and do what you think. This will vanish on it's own by time. Soon.

comments.author: Frequent-Motor-492
comments.body: Just gotta wait until the pearl clutchers find something else to make them feel pious.

comments.author: SeasawPhilosopher
comments.body: Make it fun and not look like slop and no one will give two shits how you made it. You really think gamers are going to avoid playing something fun becuse of virtue? Nah, players don’t give a fuck outside of virtue signaling online. Good games will attract players, end of story. The trouble is it’s really really hard to make a good game that retains players even with AI helping you.

comments.author: Bratchan
comments.body: Here's the issue. Right now we have a flood gate open of slop that is pouring onto steam. It's everyone mimic a game etc.  Games unless you been working on the game design for a while will take months even with AI to fine tune. Those games that someone has taken the time with will push past that issue. So we have to wait for the 'hype' and the slop to go calm down. So then AI games that people really put the time into and work will start to push up.

replies.author: GulbrandrGameStudios
replies.body: Exactly. I remember Google Play used to be flooded with the same low-quality, human pulp games. Now, the number of those games seems to be decreasing.

replies.author: MadJagStudios
replies.body: We have very different experiences of the play store lol

comments.author: Destituted
comments.body:
There is a guy that leaves bad reviews for any game made with Godot that people just joke about, which is eventually what these antis will be reduced to.

As others have said, if your game is polished and good then the real reviews will drown out the negative over time but it may still be a speed bump for visibility for now.

comments.author: Ichi_Wang
comments.body:
As others have said be honest about your use of A.I in the game; But also, release a demo of your game. 

If it's fun and engaging people will probably forgive/forget the A.I thing. If its not fun, A.I use or not ain't gonna help it.

comments.author: JorgitoEstrella
comments.body: I thought a refunded game didn't count for the rating

comments.author: Fun-Mission-6068
comments.body: If you don't want people to refund it because it uses AI, you should probably just be upfront and obvious in disclosing that it uses AI so they don't buy it and get jebaited.

comments.author: GulbrandrGameStudios
comments.body:
No worries. AI haters are just haters and nothing more. They don’t play games, and they don’t buy them either. I published my game and haven’t received any anti-AI comments or refund requests because of AI (on steam).

The main problem is promotion. Publishers and journalists are really, really, really scared of the anti-AI crowd, so they avoid touching any game that involved AI, no matter whether it was used for generated images, music, or even code.

comments.author: satorinano
comments.body: I couldn't care less. I care if its fun. I suspect enough people would too. The AI antis are a minority.

comments.author: Tarl2323
comments.body: You can't. If you're looking to make money, do something else. Your only option is just to put it out there and eat the shit. Even if you don't use AI, someone will accuse you of using AI. You might as well just do it and lie.

comments.author: zenmatrix83
comments.body: there will be haters with ai or not, and people who try to refund and do bad reviews anyways. gamers are some of the greediest people, alot are against ai because ai was partially trained on works that no one gave permissions to and they consider it stealing, but alot of those same people pirate video games movies and anything else they can.

comments.author: tunelesspaper
comments.body: My plan is to lean hard into AI art and make it a selling point. Then I’ll offer a premium content pack that replaces all the beautiful AI art in the game with 100% verifiably human hand-drawn art. It’ll be whatever shit I can smear on a cocktail napkin and scan in, but the anti-AI purists will have their vegan meal option if they want it.

comments.author: ichivictus
comments.body: I just don't disclose and make my game good enough that it is not obvious.
